## My Thinking

I've farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life, same as my father before me. I have 10 mu of contracted land. There's really no question about what I grow — wheat in the winter, corn in the summer. Everyone here does this rotation. The land is flat, the water is underground, and these two crops pay the bills. I wouldn't try something new at my age on land I depend on.

For wheat, I'll plant in mid-October after the corn comes off. I'll go to the township seed station and buy Jimai 22 or Kenong 199 — whichever they have more of. These improved seeds yield better than the old ones, and the extension station recommends them, so I trust them. I'll do rotary tillage before planting, broadcast compound fertilizer into the soil, then top-dress urea at jointing stage. The winters here are dry and spring rains aren't reliable, so I'll pump from the well four times: once before freeze-up, then at greening, jointing, and heading. I'll spray herbicide in November and a fungicide when the heads come out.

For corn, I seed right after the wheat comes off in June — no time to waste. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid, same as the last several years. I'll let the no-tillage seeder go directly into the stubble — saves me time and my back isn't what it was. Summer rains help, but I'll irrigate twice if needed. I top-dress urea at the big bell stage. One herbicide spray early and one pest spray if the aphids get bad.

I hire the village machinery cooperative for seeding and harvest on both crops. I do the fertilizing and spraying myself.
